what: the concrete stair east of the house, as one average step
where_it_stands: John, 2026-08-14. The bottom step is level with the floor of the upper level, 10.45 m, and the flight stands three of its own widths further east than the slide down the bank had left it. Moved 3.60 m due east. The height, the bearing and the placement across the flight were not touched.
how_that_was_applied: cabin.js puts the roof at (-34.17, -7.03) turned 18.2 deg, 8.17 m across the ridge by 8.49 along, eaves included. The foot sits 6.27 m east of the roof centre in the cabin's own frame and 5.89 m south, so it is off the south-east corner of the house and clear of the upper deck.
what_is_left_of_the_photograph_fit: nothing. It fixed how far along the flight the foot sat, and the foot is John's now. The bearing, the placement across the flight, the tread and the rise are all John's, or solved against the ground from them.
not_measured: the width, taken as 1.2 m, and the difference between one step and the next, which John says is real and this does not know
steps_and_tread_are_John's: nineteen steps, tread about ten inches. Those two were never fitted.

bottom.ground_m_note: The floor of the upper level, off cabin.js. John, 2026-08-14: the bottom step is level with it. The lidar here is 12.65, so the bottom step is 2.20 m under the bank and the carve takes the bank away.

the_slope: The tread is John's ten inches. The rise was solved to land the top step on the ground when the foot stood 3.60 m west of here, and it was kept when the flight moved east. 33.4 deg, a 6.6 in riser on a 10 in tread.
the_ground_is_cut_for_it: The whole flight now runs under the lidar bank — 2.20 m under at the foot and 1.02 m at the head. stairCarve cuts the ground down to the underside of the treads along the flight and 0.3 m past each end, and leaves it alone elsewhere, so what is drawn is a channel 1.5 m wide dug into the bank with the stair standing in it. It only cuts, never fills. The lidar cannot see a cut this narrow: its cells are 1.14 m and the flight is 1.2 m wide, so a real cut for a real stair is smoothed away in the bake and has to be put back here.
